STILL not a clean bill of health, but for a smaller reason than before. Three committed scenarios, all green and all RUNNING (no #[ignore], no scheduled-deep-checks exclusion): the named sibling-cohort fold, restore_blocks_by_ids_omits_the_1884_ancestor_chain_restore (the #3818 reproducer) and restore_blocks_by_ids_skips_a_live_block_the_single_path_refuses (the #3838 reproducer), both now regression guards. #3818 was: the batch cleared deleted_at DOWNWARD only, skipping the #1884 restore_deleted_ancestor_chain the single path runs, so a block restored under a separately-tombstoned parent came back live under an invisible one — absent from the tree render AND from list_trash. Mirroring restore_all_deleted_inner is what hid it: the all-variant restores every tombstone, so the upward walk is vacuous THERE. Fixed by calling the helper once per root (idempotent + op-free, so overlapping chains collapse) and rooting the inheritance recompute at the topmost restored ancestor. #3838 was the mirror image of the #3819 purge asymmetry, left standing one function away: a LIVE input id fell out of the deleted_at IS NOT NULL root filter and was SILENTLY SKIPPED where restore_block_inner REFUSES it, a permanent batch-vs-fold output divergence. Non-destructive (a skipped restore leaves the block tombstoned) but real; fixed the way #3819 was — REFUSE, raising restore_block_inner's "block '<id>' is not deleted" message byte-for-byte rather than filtering — byte-for-byte requires ORDER BY je.key on the probe, since the fold names the first live id in INPUT order while an unordered LIMIT 1 names an index-order one (the same correction was applied to #3819's purge probe, which shipped unordered). MISSING ids are still silently dropped by design, as on the purge path. STILL UNCOVERED, and the only remaining known UNINTENDED gap (the missing-id output divergence — batch Ok(0) vs fold NotFound — is also unpinned, but is deliberate and shared identically with the purge pair): this path skips the in-tx rederive_page_and_space_ids refresh restore_block_inner runs; neither the ancestor-chain nor the live-id fixture can see it (seeded page_id/space_id are already correct on both arms) — catching it needs a scenario that MOVES a block while it is soft-deleted. Note what that means for the oracle: #3856 was a genuine batch-vs-fold DIVERGENCE and batch ≡ fold still held, because the arms' op_log and SQL state agreed and only the per-space LoroDoc differed — CRDT state is outside everything this harness snapshots, so widening a scenario would not have found it either. Both are pinned instead by absolute-invariant tests in the same scenario file (restore_block_inner_fans_the_restored_subtree_to_the_engine, its restore_blocks_by_ids_inner sibling, and restore_all_deleted_inner_fans_the_restored_subtree_to_the_engine), which read the engine directly and assert engine/SQL agreement for the ancestor, the seed AND a descendant after a local restore, rather than arm equality
